answers.rationale: Her history does not support an automatic open-jaw rule. She repeatedly compares airfare, one-way rental fees, airport timing, materials, and backtracking; she chose open-jaw only when the total operational case was better. This route needs the same three-way comparison.

She has used open-jaw routing when it removes meaningful end-of-trip backtracking, but has retained same-airport returns when connections, fees, or timing make them cleaner. The MCI/STL decision should remain contingent on all-in cost, the drop fee, and the 70-minute connection rather than applying a fixed rule.

For western regional loops, she weighs winter roads, material volume, mileage reimbursement, airport reliability, and one-way rental pricing. Her history supports evaluating open-jaw, round-trip, and driving rather than assuming either open-jaw or driving is always correct.

She values prior-day arrival for mandatory early or high-risk starts, but has accepted same-day nonstop arrivals when the first obligation has genuine cushion and the added hotel night is not justified. A 10:25 arrival for a 2:00 informal prep conversation supports Monday travel, with Sunday reserved if the prep becomes mandatory or moves earlier.
